Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaHealth Hospitals Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to request through the phone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaHealth Hospitals' financial results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the Q3. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on six key aspects: Factors affecting operating margin (e.g., revenue growth, cost control), Strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter/year, Initiatives to improve operating margin, Same-facility admissions and patient day growth (YoY and QoQ), Impact of value-based care contracts on reimbursement, and Capital expenditure guidance for the next quarter/year.

These aspects underscore the strength of our results and our path forward. Let me begin with our strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year. Thank you, colleagues, for that context. As we look ahead, I'm pleased to share our strategic priorities and outlook for the remainder of fiscal 2024 and into Q1 2025. VitaHealth Hospitals remains laser-focused on delivering sustainable growth in a dynamic healthcare landscape, where we're navigating favorable tailwinds like pent-up demand for elective procedures and Medicare Advantage expansion, alongside headwinds such as persistent labor inflation and CMS reimbursement pressures.

Let me start with our core strategic pillars, which are designed to drive mid-teens adjusted EBITDA growth while expanding our market share to 4.5% nationally by year-end—from 4.1% today—positioning us competitively against peers like HCA Healthcare and Tenet Healthcare.

First, operational excellence and margin expansion. We've made significant strides in our "VitaOptimize" initiative, leveraging predictive analytics from our partnership with Cerner and Google Cloud to optimize staffing and bed utilization. In Q3, this drove a 250-basis-point improvement in our case-mix-adjusted cost per case, bringing our system-wide adjusted EBITDA margin to 13.2%—up from 11.8% a year ago. Looking forward, we expect to sustain 12.5-14% margins through the year, with Q4 guidance reflecting a 5-7% sequential increase in patient days to 1.2 million, fueled by a 9% YoY rise in inpatient volumes and 12% in outpatient encounters. Our same-facility revenue per admission is projected to grow 4-5%, supported by favorable payer mix shifts—commercial insurance now at 58% of revenues, up from 55%—despite a 2.3% CMS IPPS cut for FY2025 that we'll offset through acuity management and denials prevention tech.

Second, network expansion and de novo growth. We're accelerating our footprint in high-growth Sunbelt markets, where population inflows and aging demographics are outpacing the national average. In Q4, we'll break ground on a 150-bed acute-care hospital in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, our third de novo in Texas since 2022, targeting $120 million in annualized EBITDA run-rate by 2026. Regionally, the Southeast remains our powerhouse, with Florida facilities posting 15% YoY revenue growth on 11% volume increases, driven by Medicare Advantage penetration now at 32% locally—mirroring trends at peers like Universal Health Services. Conversely, in the Northeast, we're prudently rightsizing under two legacy assets amid New York state certificate-of-need bottlenecks, but expect flat-to-2% growth there as we pivot to ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs). Overall, M&A remains opportunistic; we've allocated $750 million for tuck-in acquisitions, with two LOIs signed for micro-hospitals in Arizona and Georgia, emphasizing high-ROI assets yielding 12-15% unlevered IRR.

Third, advancing value-based care and digital transformation. With 45% of our lives now in risk-bearing arrangements—up from 35% last year—we're deepening partnerships with ACOs like Privia Health and expanding our VitaCare population health platform. This has already delivered $45 million in shared savings in the first three quarters, and we forecast $100 million for full-year 2024. On the tech front, we're rolling out AI-driven tools from Nuance and PathAI across 80% of our 45 hospitals by year-end, targeting a 15-20% reduction in length-of-stay for high-acuity cases like orthopedics and cardiology. Telehealth volumes are stabilizing at 18% of visits post-pandemic, but we're innovating with hybrid virtual care models compliant with the No Surprises Act, projecting 25% growth in Q4 as we integrate with Apple Health and Fitbit ecosystems for remote monitoring.

Fourth, workforce stabilization. Labor remains our largest opex at 52% of costs, with RN turnover down to 14% from 22% two years ago via our "VitaRetain" program—$50 million invested in sign-on bonuses, tuition reimbursement, and AI scheduling. We expect wage inflation to moderate to 4-5% in Q4 from 7%, aligning with industry benchmarks from Advisory Board data.

Outlook and Guidance. For Q4, we guide revenues to $2.85-2.95 billion, up 8-10% YoY; adjusted EBITDA of $380-410 million, implying 13.5% margins; and EPS of $1.25-1.45. Full-year 2024 guidance is tightened to revenues of $11.6-11.8 billion (9% growth), EBITDA of $1.55-1.60 billion (14% growth at midpoint), and free cash flow of $950 million. Entering 2025, we see 7-9% revenue growth, with tailwinds from elective procedure normalization (now at 95% of pre-COVID levels) and potential tailwinds from a bipartisan drug pricing bill. Risks include ransomware threats—we're 100% cyber-insured and air-gapped critical systems—and supply chain volatility for ortho implants, which we're mitigating via Vizient GPO contracts.

In summary, our priorities are yielding tangible results, positioning VitaHealth for compounding growth in an industry ripe for consolidation. We're not just managing costs; we're building a resilient, tech-enabled network that's the partner of choice for payers and patients alike.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial results, including the other key aspects like operating margins, volume growth, value-based care impacts, margin improvement initiatives, and capex guidance.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael, and good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. I'll now dive into our operating margin performance for Q3, which came in at 8.7%, up 220 basis points year-over-year from 6.5% and marking our strongest quarterly result since pre-pandemic levels. This expansion reflects disciplined execution across both revenue growth levers and cost control measures, even amidst persistent industry headwinds like labor inflation and supply chain volatility. Let me break it down step-by-step, with some color on the key drivers, regional nuances, and our strategic initiatives.

Starting with the top line, net revenue for the quarter was $2.4 billion, an increase of 6.8% compared to the same period last year, outpacing the 4.2% industry average reported by Kaufman Hall's National Hospital Flash Report. Admissions rose 4.1% to 145,000, fueled by a 7% rebound in elective procedures—think orthopedics, cardiology, and oncology—as pent-up demand materialized post-COVID backlogs. Our case mix index, or CMI, held steady at 1.85, benefiting from higher-acuity cases like our expanded TAVR and robotic-assisted surgeries, which now represent 15% of surgical volume across our 45-hospital footprint.

Payer mix remains a bright spot: commercial insurance penetration improved to 52% from 49%, driven by favorable renegotiations with Blue Cross Blue Shield plans in our Southeast markets, yielding a 3.2% net revenue per admission increase. Medicare, at 38% of mix, saw modest reimbursement pressure from CMS's FY24 IPPS update, which cut payments by 2.7% after standardization, but we offset this through our value-based care contracts—now covering 25% of Medicare lives—delivering shared savings of $18 million in the quarter. Outpatient revenue surged 12%, shifting 28% of our volume to higher-margin ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs) and hospital outpatient departments (HOPDs), aligning with the industry's migration away from lower-margin inpatient stays.

On the cost side, total operating expenses were $2.19 billion, representing 91.3% of net revenue. Labor costs, our largest bucket at 54% of revenue, increased 5.8% year-over-year due to ongoing RN shortages and premium pay—wage inflation averaged 4.5% amid a 3.2% national healthcare vacancy rate per NSI Nursing Solutions data. However, we contained this through our "CareSync Workforce Optimization" initiative, leveraging AI-driven scheduling from Cerner and ShiftMed partnerships, which reduced agency labor from 12% to 8% of total RN hours and improved fill rates to 96%.

Supply expenses, at 22% of revenue, were up 6.2% from drug and implant inflation—Ozempic and similar GLP-1s drove pharmacy costs higher by 11%, echoing challenges at peers like HCA Healthcare. We countered with our Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) strategy via Vizient, securing 8-10% discounts on high-volume ortho implants and locking in 18-month contracts for commodity supplies. This, combined with RFID-enabled inventory management at 32 of our facilities, trimmed supply cost per case by 3.4%.

Other key cost controls included a 15% reduction in professional fees through in-sourcing radiology reads via our PACS system upgrade and bad debt expense stabilizing at 2.1% of revenue, thanks to enhanced revenue cycle management (RCM) with Waystar's AI denial prevention tools—our days in A/R now sit at 42, versus an industry peer median of 48.

Regionally, our Sunbelt markets—Florida, Texas, and the Carolinas, representing 62% of EBITDA—drove 65% of margin expansion, with operating margins hitting 11.2% on 9% volume growth from migration-driven population booms and Medicaid redetermination tailwinds adding 50,000 covered lives. In contrast, our Northeast facilities faced 1.5% margin compression from New York and Massachusetts rate regulations and higher unionized labor costs (up 6.8%), but we're mitigating via a $150 million divestiture of underperforming assets there, expected to close Q1 next year.

Strategically, these factors position us well for sustained 9-10% margins in FY24. We're accelerating ASC buildouts—eight new centers slated for 2024, targeting 20% EBITDA margins akin to United Surgical Partners International (USPI)—and piloting bundled payment models with UnitedHealth's Optum for ortho episodes, which early data shows boosting CMI by 0.12 points. Tech-wise, our Epic MyChart telehealth integration lifted virtual visits 25% quarter-over-quarter, enhancing access without fixed-cost bed expansions.

Looking forward, we see Q4 operating margins of 8.5-9.0%, assuming stable CMS rates and moderating labor inflation to 3.5%. Risks include potential Medicare Advantage clawbacks, as seen with Humana's recent star rating hits, but our payer diversification and $500 million share repurchase authorization underscore confidence in our trajectory.

Net income for the quarter was $175 million, or $1.20 per share. Building on that, let me address same-facility admissions and patient days growth, both year-over-year (YoY) and quarter-over-quarter (QoQ). These are critical leading indicators for our Healthcare Services platform, reflecting organic demand at our existing 45 hospitals and freestanding ERs across key states. We're reporting these on a same-facility basis, excluding divestitures and new builds that ramped earlier this year. This gives a clean view of underlying performance.

For Q3 2024, same-facility admissions grew 4.2% YoY and 1.8% QoQ, while same-facility patient days expanded 5.1% YoY and 2.3% QoQ. These figures mark our strongest quarterly volume growth since late 2021, outpacing our historical three-year CAGR of 2.8% for admissions and the industry median of 3.1% per Kaufman Hall.

On a YoY basis, admissions growth was broad-based, with inpatient admissions up 3.8%—driven by a 12% surge in elective orthopedics and cardiology procedures, now 28% of total volume, up from 24%. This reflects pent-up demand clearing, with wait times for joint replacements down 35% since late 2022, thanks to $250 million in OR expansions including da Vinci Xi at 45 facilities.

Behavioral health admissions jumped 7.2% YoY, fueled by Optum and Teladoc partnerships adding 120 beds in Florida and Arizona. Oncology up 5.4%, aligned with American Cancer Society trends. Patient days grew faster at 5.1% YoY due to a 42 basis point CMI increase to 1.68 from higher acuity like sepsis and neuro cases. ALOS ticked to 4.7 days from 4.6, pressured by ICU utilization at 88%.

Regionally, Sunbelt—Texas, Florida, Georgia at 52% of beds—led with 6.1% admissions growth from 1.2 million net migrants. Midwest/Northeast grew 1.9%, hit by Medicaid redeterminations.

Sequentially, admissions rose 1.8% from Q2 as flu eased, patient days 2.3% with acuity up in heart failure and septicemia DRGs. Observation-to-admission conversions improved 15% via Epic and Nuance tools.

These stem from our "Volume Velocity" strategy: digital front door up 28% scheduling, workforce optimization holding ratios at 1:4.8, and 42% Medicare lives in ACO REACH 2.0 with 4-star ratings.

Headwinds: labor at 32% revenue, CMS 2.9% IPPS cut, payer mix 32% Medicare/28% Medicaid/32% commercial/8% managed Medicare. Full-year guide: admissions 3.5-4.5%, patient days 4-5%, upside from $1.2B M&A.

Next, the impact of value-based care contracts on reimbursement has been transformative. VBC ties payments to quality, outcomes, efficiency, and satisfaction—HEDIS, CMS Stars, readmissions penalties. Our 35+ contracts span Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, commercial like UnitedHealthcare, Elevance, Humana.

VBC is 38% of net patient revenue, up from 28% YoY, $1.2B of $3.2B quarterly top line growing 45% vs. 7% overall, ahead of CMS's 2030 mandate.

Medicare Advantage VBC 52% mix, $625M Q3, MSSP Track 3 ACOs $42M shared savings up 28% on 96% quality. Commercial 30% $360M with 12% bonuses on bundles. Medicaid 18% $215M fastest growth via CalAIM, Texas programs, 15-20% above FFS on SDOH.

VBC boosts reimbursement per case 8.2% YTD to $15,400 vs. FFS $14,200, EBITDA margins 12.1% vs. 9.8%. Avoided $18M penalties, readmissions to 14.2% down 18%, banked $31M incentives including $12M Humana lump-sum.

Investments $75M in Epic Healthy Planet, Innovaccer compressed cash 3-4%, but HCC stabilized at 95%.

Regionally: Northeast 48% VBC revenue via BCBS MA, 22% readmission cuts; Southeast 32% with 50% MA in Miami; Midwest Medicaid 25% PMPM up 17%; West 28%.

Tech: $150M data lake, AI risk models up HCC 14%, Care Navigation Hubs cut LOS 0.8 days, HCAHPS 85th percentile.

VBC our margin engine, 1% quality gain = $15-20M upside, targeting 50% mix by 2026. Guide $180-210M FY savings, Q4 up 10% QoQ.

Turning to our initiatives to improve operating margin—a core pillar targeting 8-9% by FY2025 end. Q3 consolidated at 6.2% up 110 bps YoY from 5.1%, strongest pre-pandemic. Four levers: labor productivity, supply chain, revenue cycle, clinical throughput.

Labor 52% costs: "Apex Flex Workforce" model—wait, our "VitaFlex" cut turnover to 12% from 25% peak. AI Epic/ShiftMed RN HPPD to 7.2 down 8%, $45M Q3 savings 25 bps in FL/TX 60% beds. Travel nurses down 65% QoQ to 5%, internal float 1,200. Expect 50-75 bps H2 lift as vacancies to 9%.

Sunbelt 92% occupancy.

Supply 22% revenue: Vizient GPO 12% YTD savings $120M. Ortho Zimmer Biomet 18% per case cut, 340B $28M Q3 40 bps. Vendor to 1,200 SKUs, McKesson RFID 15% carrying cut. Stabilize 20.5% revenue 75 bps 2025.

RCM: revenue/admission $14,200 up 4.2%, AR 42 days, UiPath bots denials to 4.2% down 35% $65M recovered. Commercial OPCMI parity 2.5% lift, TX Medicaid 5%. Employed docs 65% of 2,500 drive 12% outpatient.

Throughput: ALOS 4.3 from 4.7, CMI 1.85. Electives 18% OR 68%, da Vinci complications down 22% LOS -0.8 $2,100/case. Epic Hyperdrive discharge delays -25%, telehealth 22% visits readmits -14%.

Sunbelt 15% procedural FL, Midwest bundles 11% margins. Synergies 160 bps Q3. Guide Q4 7.0-7.5%, 2025 8.5%, ROIC >12%, $500M buyback.

Finally, capital expenditure guidance. FY24 through Q3 $1.15B toward $1.2-1.3B, $450M facilities, $350M equipment, $250M IT.

Q4 $325-375M up 10-15% QoQ: facilities $150-170M ASCs DFW/Tampa $120M, NE ED $30M; equipment $100-110M Siemens MRI/da Vinci $60M; IT $65-75M Epic AI/cyber/virtual $50M; maint $15-20M.

60% Sunbelt.

FY25 raised $1.3-1.45B 6-6.5% revenue: facilities $600-650M 10 ASCs/micros 500 beds oncology/behav; equip $400-450M Varian; IT $250-300M RCM/tele-ICU; maint $50-100M. IRR >15%, ESG IRA credits.

Risks construction shortages, $500M revolver. Accretive for 300-400 bps margin expansion.

We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Raj Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Heart Failure Care Pathway has shown promising results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, which has seen 25% growth in virtual visits quarter-over-quarter via Epic MyChart integration.

Following that, Tom will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including CareSync Workforce Optimization, which reduced agency labor and boosted fill rates, and our supply chain GPO strategy with Vizient, yielding 8-10% discounts and 3.4% lower cost per case. These have resulted in significant cost savings, contributing over 100 basis points to margins.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez for an overview of our innovation efforts.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Tom. We are committed to driving innovation across our organization. We are investing in new technologies and partnerships to improve patient care, enhance efficiency, and create new revenue streams. Our current projects include AI-driven predictive analytics from Nuance and PathAI for risk stratification, and telehealth expansions with remote monitoring integrations addressing key healthcare challenges like labor shortages and readmission risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Elena. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the specific cost savings achieved through the implementation of CareSync Workforce Optimization?

Tom Hargrove:
Thanks, John. CareSync, powered by Cerner and ShiftMed AI scheduling, reduced agency labor from 12% to 8% of RN hours, improved fill rates to 96%, and cut RN hours per patient day by 8% to 7.2 in acute beds. This delivered $45 million in savings in Sunbelt facilities alone, equating to 25 basis points of margin expansion, while aligning with CMS staffing benchmarks and supporting high occupancy without quality trade-offs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez:
What are your expectations for the impact of telehealth on your revenue and patient access?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Good question, Emily. Telehealth now accounts for 22% of visits, stabilizing post-pandemic but growing 25% QoQ through Epic MyChart and hybrid models compliant with No Surprises Act. It enhances access, reduces readmissions by 14%, and delivers 10% margins on virtual encounters. We project 25% Q4 growth with Apple Health integrations, shifting low-acuity volume outpatient, boosting revenue per encounter 15% while cutting fixed bed costs—key for our 18% overall telehealth stabilization target.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Can you provide more details on your plans for investing in new technologies and partnerships?

Elena Vasquez:
Absolutely, David. Our $250-300 million FY25 IT CapEx targets AI/ML from Nuance, PathAI for 15-20% LOS reductions in ortho/cardio, and Epic Hyperdrive for RCM aiming 98% clean claims. Partnerships with Privia Health ACOs and Optum bundles deepen VBC, while Cerner/Google Cloud predictive tools optimize staffing. These address labor shortages, with tele-ICU expansions countering RN gaps, targeting 300 bps EBITDA lift and peer-leading utilization.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's questions.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the VitaHealth Hospitals Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
